extractedText: US Resumes Strikes on Iran After Hormuz Vessel Attack, Vows "Price to Pay"International|Published 2026.07.12. 09:37:07|By Lim Hye-rin|Summary|SaveAAAReuters/Yonhap NewsThe United States has resumed airstrikes against Iran, saying a merchant vessel passing through the Strait of Hormuz was attacked by Iran.The U.S. Central Command announced on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) on the 11th that "at 7:15 p.m. Eastern Time, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) blatantly attacked the Cyprus-flagged container ship 'M/V GFS Galaxy' as it transited the Strait of Hormuz," adding that "units under Central Command launched their third strike this week."According to Central Command, the attack left one civilian crew member missing and caused a fire aboard the vessel. The engine room was also severely damaged, leaving the ship unable to continue sailing, it was reported.The United States criticized Iran for again passing up the chance to comply with a previous memorandum of understanding (MOU), even as it was responsible for the earlier attack on a merchant vessel. It said, "The United States is continuously degrading Iran's ability to attack civilian crews and merchant vessels freely transiting the Strait of Hormuz, making Iran pay a heavy price." It also explained that the strike was carried out at the direction of the commander in chief.U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also shared Central Command's announcement, saying, "Iran made a terrible choice," and "Now they will pay the price."Foreign media reported that explosions followed in various parts of Iran after the strikes. Russia's TASS news agency, citing Iranian media, reported that explosions were heard in the southern regions of Assaluyeh and Bushehr. Assaluyeh is home to Iran's largest oil refining facility, while Bushehr hosts Iran's only commercial nuclear power plant.Reuters, citing Iran's state IRIB broadcaster, also reported that three explosions were reported in the southern port city of Bandar Abbas and two in Sirik.Just before the U.S. announcement of the strikes, the IRGC declared a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, citing vessels attempting to transit through illegal routes.The United States and Iran have continued their conflict over control of the Strait of Hormuz even after signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) last month. The United States also struck southern Iran over two days on the 8th, and in response Iran launched retaliatory attacks targeting major U.S. military facilities in Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain, with armed clashes between the two sides continuing.#Iran#StraitOfHormuz#USMilitary#IRGC#MiddleEast#Airstrikes#HegsethOriginal reporting by Lim Hye-rin for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
